{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
Christian, also recorded as Christine or Christan Davidson, was probably born about 1752. This remains an uncertain estimate from the reported 1772 marriage and her documented motherhood by 1774; no baptism for her has been identified.

The retained banns-and-marriages citation records Christan Davidson and [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] at Livingston on or after 7 November 1772.<ref name="Marriage1772">Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers, Banns and Marriages, parish 669, reference 20/81, frame 497, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ retained ScotlandsPeople citation], accessed 3 September 2026; Christan Davidson and Thomas Glasgow on or after 7 November 1772. No original newly inspected.</ref> Their son [[Glasgow-1452|Nathaniel Glasgow]] was baptised 2 January 1774 at Livingston, with Thomas Glasgow and Christine Davidson named as parents.<ref name="Nathaniel1774">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RG-M2G record X1RG-M2G], accessed 26 August 2026; Nathaniel Glasgow, baptism 2 January 1774, parents Thomas Glasgow and Christine Davidson. Compare held Findmypast derivatives [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685841078&tab=this R_685841078] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692405171&tab=this R_692405171]; one baptism, original uninspected.</ref>

The same parental household is recorded for [[Glasgow-1448|Janet]], baptised 2 February 1777; [[Glasgow-1451|Catharine]], born 20 August and baptised 31 August 1780 at Blackburne; [[Glasgow-1453|Mary]], recorded with variant 1783/1784 baptism dates; [[Glasgow-1449|Thomas]], born 26 April 1787 according to the Whitburn OPR derivative; and [[Glasgow-1450|Peter]] in the maintained 1790 child account.<ref name="FamilyChildren">Held Findmypast parish derivatives: Janet, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685844147&tab=this R_685844147] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403113&tab=this R_692403113]; Catharine, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4152175&tab=this OPR 669/1 item 4, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4152175]; Mary, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685840887&tab=this R_685840887], [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403782&tab=this R_692403782] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4152265&tab=this SCOT/OPR/BAP/4152265]; Thomas, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4171361&tab=this OPR 673/1 item 3 page 61, SCOT/OPR/BAP/4171361]. Parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson are named; original registers uninspected. Variants describe related parish evidence and are not independent confirmations.</ref> These links do not settle the children's separately qualified adult identities.

Christian probably died on 5 November 1795, the date shared by the Livingston memorial transcriptions. They give her age as 43 or 45; neither is used to replace the existing approximate birth with an exact year.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI" /> The fuller inscription explicitly calls her Janet's mother and Thomas's wife, supporting her existing maternal link to Janet at 97% confident.

== Research Notes ==
=== Maternity and the existing household ===
Janet's 97% is the first individual rating of an existing mother attachment, not a new attachment or a measured confidence gain. The full parental couple in the 1777 baptism and the memorial's explicit mother wording support the family without inferring maternity solely from a father's wife. The father and mother grades share the same family-identity argument, not independent confirmation.

Nathaniel's 1774 record is the first child in the held sequence, not proof of an eldest son. Catharine's exact 1780 parent fields and the later children's full couple are distinct parish-event evidence; copies of each event are not independent witnesses. Mary’s Livingston/Whitburn and 1783/1784 variants remain unresolved, as do the younger Thomas's differing birth/baptism labels. A separate 1793 Peter entry names a labourer Thomas but no mother; this does not attach that child to Christian.

=== Janet's identity and parental roles ===
The held Livingston baptism names Janet Glasgow, Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson on 2 February 1777; one companion gives Livingston residence. These are two indexes of one event, not separate children.<ref name="Janet1777">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685844147&tab=this R_685844147] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_692403113&tab=this R_692403113], Janet Glasgow, baptism 2 February 1777, Livingston, parents Thomas Glasgow and Christian Davidson; held inspected derivatives, original register uninspected.</ref> The memorial explicitly calls Christian Janet's mother and Thomas her father. The full couple, family memorial and chronology support 97% for each existing parent placement. The father's former 43% possible grade is superseded; the mother's 97% is her first individual rating, not a new maternal attachment or a measured rise from an invented earlier percentage.

Age 76 with death in 1853 is compatible with baptism near birth in 1777, although baptism need not have been in infancy. The conflicting 1873/76 combination implies birth around 1797, after the named mother's 1795 death, so those digits cannot all be correct for the same daughter. A correct later death year with a wrong age remains possible. The combined correlation favours 16 October 1853, with 1873 remaining an alternative.

The inherited Bridgeton, Kincardineshire birthplace remains unverified and is retained as a field-level claim, not asserted by the Livingston baptism. The fuller inscription's “Janet Glasgow, Blackburn” may identify a locality; it does not prove a married surname. No husband, marriage or descendants are inferred. An earlier about-1780 birth estimate and firm unsourced parent statement were superseded by the existing before-2-February-1777 bound and the dated assessments. The present family inference replaces the older blanket hold; it does not silently settle the place or surname questions.

=== Memorial readings and source limits ===
The preferred readings come from a combined interpretation of held derivatives, not a new stone reading or source fetch. One Findmypast version gives Thomas's death as 22 July 1831, aged 85; Christian Davidson, 5 November 1795, aged 43; son Peter, 12 September 1810, aged 19; and daughter Janet, 16 October 1853, aged 76. It also names grandchildren Mary Russell, who died in infancy, Jessie Russell, 11 July 1845, aged 20, another Jessie Russell, 8 February 1851, aged ten months, and James B. Russell, 22 April 1854, aged nineteen months.

The fuller companion says Janet Glasgow, Blackburn, erected the memorial for her mother Christian Davidson, who died 5 November 1795 aged 45; Thomas Glasgow her father, 22 May 1831 aged 85; and Peter her brother, 12 September 1819 aged 48. It gives the above Janet's death as 16 October 1873 aged 76, the infant Jessie's date as 8 February 1831, and James B. Russell's year as 185*. These differing month/year/age readings are retained, not harmonised into independent people or new exact facts. Repeated rows under different family names still refer to the same memorial.<ref name="LivingstonFamilyMI">Findmypast, ''Scotland Monumental Inscriptions'', Livingston family memorial, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00542646&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00542646] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511333&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511333]; compare the same inscription indexed under Janet as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00422894&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00422894] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511321&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511321], and under Peter as [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00516377&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00516377] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511329&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511329]. Held derivative transcriptions captured/reviewed 24–30 October 2026; one physical memorial, not independent witnesses. [https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 BillionGraves memorial 3399144, marker LV 106] has a competing 1851 Thomas reading and a previously blurred preview; original inscription not newly read.</ref>

BillionGraves instead indexes Thomas's death as 22 May 1851, aged 85, from which the earlier circa-1766 birth was calculated. That is not an independent birth record. The original stone and parish-register images remain uninspected for this reconciliation. A legible inscription or burial record could resolve the disputed digits, but a blanket requirement for an original does not prevent a qualified preferred interpretation of the existing family evidence. No Russell grandchild is assigned a parent profile through these readings alone.

=== Dates, prior interpretation and next evidence ===
The earlier 1752 estimate used age twenty at the structured 1772 marriage; it remains approximate. The memorial ages of 43/45 in 1795 imply different approximate birth years and are preserved, not silently reconciled. The shared 5 November 1795 death is the preferred qualified derivative reading. Husband Thomas's preferred death year is 1831 aged 85, with 22 May/22 July unresolved and the old 1851 reading retained. Daughter Janet's preferred 1853 death is correlated with her 1777 baptism and named mother's 1795 death; the later 1873/76 combination is inconsistent if all its digits are accepted, but a wrong age remains possible.

The previous unassessed Janet maternity and blanket pending-original hold are superseded only to this stated extent. The original inscription, burial evidence and parish registers could refine disputed digits and identity details; no original was newly read, no source newly fetched, and no mother's own parents, exact birth date, new spouse or live WikiTree edit is claimed. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/glasgow-1382.html#research-findings The shared family argument].
